concepts.learning_objective: Recall how the sights of sickness, age, death and a begging monk led Prince Siddhartha to seek enlightenment.
Explain how Siddhartha became the Buddha and where he preached his first sermon.

topics.title: Kisa Gotami's grief and the mustard-seed task

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Kisa Gotami's first search for medicine and how her neighbours reacted.
Explain the condition the Buddha set for the mustard-seed and the purpose behind it.
Interpret the image of the flickering city lights as a symbol of human life.
Explain why Kisa Gotami calls herself selfish in her grief and what she comes to understand.

topics.title: The Buddha's sermon on death and grief

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the similes the Buddha uses to show that all mortals are subject to death.
Explain why the Buddha says lamentation brings no peace and how peace of mind is obtained.

topics.title: Language and style of the text

concepts.learning_objective: Rephrase the old-fashioned words and expressions of the text in current English.
Explain how semicolons join closely related clauses and split such a sentence into simple sentences.
Recall the meanings of key words glossed in the chapter.

topics.title: Grief in modern texts compared with the sermon

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the feelings of grief and the ways of helping a grieving person described in the guide.
Compare Amitai Etzioni's experience of grief in 'Good Grief' with the Buddha's teaching.
